14:T5278,<p>很多網站都有「用 Google 登入」的按鈕，那是 OAuth 2.0。後來我要讓 server 每天定時讀一份 Google Calendar，執行時沒有使用者在登入。OAuth 的每個請求都代表一個按過「允許」的使用者，所以 server 要用 OAuth，就得先找一個人授權，之後一直借用他的身分。這樣做得到，可是那個人一撤銷授權，或 token 失效，server 就讀不到了。要讀的 calendar 不屬於哪個使用者的時候，用 app 自己的身分比較合適，也就是 Service Account。</p>
<p>GCP 有三種 credential，各自用不同的身分發請求。</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>Credential</th><th>用誰的身分</th><th>用途</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>OAuth 2.0 Client ID</td><td>真人使用者</td><td>讓人登入你的 app，代他存取他的資料</td></tr><tr><td>Service Account</td><td>你的 app 自己</td><td>機器對機器，沒有使用者參與</td></tr><tr><td>API Key</td><td>誰的都不用，前端後端都一樣</td><td>呼叫 Maps 這類公開的 Google API</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>選的時候依序問：</p>
<ul>
<li>要一個真人按下「允許」→ <strong>OAuth 2.0 Client ID</strong>。</li>
<li>像 Maps 這種公開 API，不需要任何人的身分 → <strong>API Key</strong>，後端呼叫也一樣。</li>
<li>你的 app 用自己的身分去做事 → <strong>Service Account</strong>。</li>
</ul>
<h2>OAuth 2.0 Client ID：代表使用者發請求</h2>
<p>我是在做 Google 登入的時候碰到它的。那是 One Tap 的彈出視窗，Medium 也有，正式名稱叫 Google Identity Services。它要我填一個 OAuth 2.0 Client ID，我就搞糊塗了，因為我已經透過 Firebase Auth 在做 Google 登入，這兩個是不同的系統嗎？</p>
<p>其實不是。兩邊底下都是 OAuth 2.0 Client ID，差別只在串接方式，而且都要使用者自己走完登入流程。兩個還可以接在一起用：讓 One Tap 拿到 credential，再交給 Firebase Auth 管理。</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// 使用者主動登入</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">google.accounts.id.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">initialize</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  client_id: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"YOUR-WEB-CLIENT-ID.apps.googleusercontent.com"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">  callback</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: (</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#FFAB70;--shiki-light:#E36209">response</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">) </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">=></span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">    // response.credential 是使用者的 ID token（一個 JWT），直接交給 Firebase</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    firebase.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">auth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">().</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">signInWithCredential</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">      firebase.auth.GoogleAuthProvider.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">credential</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(response.credential)</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    )</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">})</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>OAuth 的每個請求都代表一個使用者。</strong> 使用者登入時，如果 app 申請了 offline access，後端會拿到一個 refresh token。之後使用者不在線上，後端也能用它換新的 access token。所以只要有人同意過一次，定時跑的後端其實可以一直用 OAuth 讀他的 calendar。</p>
<p>只是 server 的權限從此綁在這個人身上。<a href="https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration">Google 的 OAuth 文件</a>列了 refresh token 會失效的情況，例如使用者撤銷授權、token 六個月沒用過。app 的 consent screen 還在 Testing 狀態的話，refresh token 七天就過期。碰到任何一種，server 就讀不到 calendar，得再請那個人登入一次。</p>
<p>建立的路徑：GCP Console → APIs &#x26; Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID → 選 application type → 設定 authorized redirect URIs。</p>
<h2>Service Account：一個虛擬員工</h2>
<p>機器對機器、中間沒有人的工作，就用這種 credential。Service Account（SA）像一個虛擬員工，有自己的身分（一個 email 地址），再替它設定權限。</p>
<p>我要讓後端用自己的身分讀<em>某一份特定</em>的 calendar，不借用任何使用者的授權，所以用 Service Account。</p>
<p>最後成功的流程：</p>
<ol>
<li>在 GCP 啟用 Calendar API。</li>
<li>建一個 Service Account，也就是之後要拿來呼叫這個 API 的身分。</li>
<li><strong>把這個 SA 的 email 加進那份 calendar 的共用名單。</strong></li>
<li>下載 SA 的 JSON key，把裡面的值放進環境變數，建立 auth client。</li>
</ol>
<p>第一次我漏了第 3 步，其他設定看起來都對，API 卻一直失敗。我用這個 SA 實測過兩種情況。第一種，calendar 存在，只是沒有共用給 SA；第二種，calendar 根本不存在。API 兩種都回 <code>404 Not Found</code>，回應內容一模一樣。這跟 <a href="https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/errors">Google 的 Calendar API 文件</a>寫的一致。所以如果 API 回了 404，先去看共用名單裡有沒有這個 SA。</p>
<p>SA 在 GCP 裡的權限再大，也讀不到沒共用給它的 calendar。就算在 GCP IAM（Identity and Access Management）給 SA 整個 project 的 Owner，結果也一樣。Calendar 是 Google Workspace 的 API（Gmail、Calendar、Drive 這一系列），讀取權限只看 calendar 自己的共用設定，GCP IAM 的角色涵蓋不到它。公司如果用 Workspace，還有另一個辦法：由 Workspace 的 super admin 開 domain-wide delegation，讓 SA 以組織裡的使用者身分存取資料。這個設定在 Workspace 的 Admin console，同樣不在 GCP IAM。</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">function</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1"> getGoogleAuth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">() {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">  // 這三個值都來自下載的 SA JSON</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> clientEmail</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> process.env.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> privateKey</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> process.env.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">?.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">replace</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#85E89D;--shiki-dark-font-weight:bold;--shiki-light:#22863A;--shiki-light-font-weight:bold">\\</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#DBEDFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">n</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">/</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">g</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">\n</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">) </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// 小心換行</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">  const</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> projectId</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> process.env.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">  return</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> new</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> google.auth.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">GoogleAuth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    credentials: { client_email: clientEmail, private_key: privateKey, project_id: projectId },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    scopes: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">],</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  })</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">export</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> function</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1"> getCalendar</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">() {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">  return</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> google.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">calendar</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({ version: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">'v3'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">, auth: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">getGoogleAuth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">() })</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">}</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<h2>API Key：公開服務的通行證</h2>
<p>最後一種最單純。API Key 用在不碰任何人私人資料的公開 Google 服務，例如 Maps。</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// 沒帶 key：HTTP 200，但 body 寫 "status": "REQUEST_DENIED"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei`</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">)</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// 帶 key：拿得到結果，每月先扣免費額度</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei&#x26;key=${</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">API_KEY</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">}`</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">)</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>這把 key 跟身分沒什麼關係，它是拿來防濫用的：rate limit、追蹤用量、計費、限制哪些網站或 app 能用。AWS API Gateway 的 API key 也是同一個用途，讓服務方計算用量跟費用。</p>
<h2>合起來看</h2>
<p>一般的全端流程三種都會用到：</p>
<ol>
<li>前端用 <strong>OAuth 2.0</strong> 讓使用者登入。</li>
<li>前端把使用者的 token 傳給後端驗證身分。</li>
<li>後端用 <strong>Service Account</strong> 呼叫 Google 的服務。</li>

<p>在 Cloud Run 上，前兩個通常不存在，ADC 會用到第三個，所以不需要 key 檔。部署時沒指定 SA 的話，Cloud Run 會掛上 Compute Engine 的預設 SA。2024-05-03 以前建立的 organization，或不屬於任何 organization 的 project，GCP 可能已經自動給這個預設 SA 整個 project 的 Editor 角色。這樣一來，有人只要攻破這個服務，就能拿它的身分改動 project 裡大部分的資源。所以最好自己建一個 SA，只給它需要的權限，再掛到服務上。</p>
<p>在自己的電腦上開發時，ADC 通常停在第 2 個，用的是開發者本人的身分。如果開發者本人就是 calendar 的擁有者，本機用他的身分一定讀得到。所以共用名單就算漏了 SA，本機也不會出錯。要等上線改用 SA 的身分，API 回了 404，才會發現 SA 漏加了。要在本機用 SA 的身分測試，可以改用 <code>gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account SA的email</code> 登入。<a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation">Google 的 impersonation 文件</a>寫明，開發者的帳號要在這個 SA 上有 <code>roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator</code> 才能這樣登入。</p>
<p><strong>部署在 Vercel 這類平台</strong>：機器不在 GCP 上，沒有 metadata server，ADC 的三個地方都是空的。這時有兩個選擇：像上面的程式碼一樣把 key 放進環境變數，或用 <a href="https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/gcp">Vercel 的 OIDC（OpenID Connect）federation</a>。走 OIDC 的話，程式在 Vercel 上會拿到一個 Vercel 簽發的 token，再拿它向 GCP 換一個 SA 的短期 token，整個過程不需要 key。</p>
<p>GCP 換發之前會檢查兩件事，所以要先設定好：</p>
<ol>
<li>這個 token 是不是 GCP 信任的來源簽的。在 GCP 建一個 Workload Identity Federation，指定信任 Vercel。</li>
<li>這個 Vercel 專案能不能用這個 SA。federation 會把 token 裡寫的團隊、專案、環境，變成一個 GCP 認得的身分（principal），例如 <code>principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/vercel/subject/owner:my-team:project:my-app:environment:production</code>。在 SA 上把 <code>roles/iam.serviceAccountUser</code> 授予這個 principal。</li>
</ol>
<p>完整的設定步驟在 <a href="https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/gcp">Vercel 的文件</a>。</p>
<h2>跟 AWS 比較</h2>
<p>AWS 跟 GCP 給服務權限的預設方向剛好相反。</p>
<p>AWS 上什麼都要先授權才能用。在 console 建一個 Lambda，預設會幫它建一個新的 execution role，只有基本的寫 log 權限，像 <code>CreateLogStream</code> 跟 <code>PutLogEvents</code>。再建第二個 Lambda，預設也會另外建一個 role，就算權限一模一樣。「這個 function 可以碰哪個服務」永遠要自己寫。</p>
<p>GCP 則是預設就先給了權限。部署 Cloud Run 時沒指定 service account 的話，每個服務都共用同一個 Compute Engine 預設 SA，而這個 SA 可能有整個 project 的 Editor 權限。有了 Editor，服務讀寫 project 裡大部分的 GCP 資源都不用另外授權。不過 Editor 是 GCP IAM 的角色，SA 要讀 calendar，還是得被加進那份 calendar 的共用名單。</p>15:T29ab,
很多網站都有「用 Google 登入」的按鈕，那是 OAuth 2.0。後來我要讓 server 每天定時讀一份 Google Calendar，執行時沒有使用者在登入。OAuth 的每個請求都代表一個按過「允許」的使用者，所以 server 要用 OAuth，就得先找一個人授權，之後一直借用他的身分。這樣做得到，可是那個人一撤銷授權，或 token 失效，server 就讀不到了。要讀的 calendar 不屬於哪個使用者的時候，用 app 自己的身分比較合適，也就是 Service Account。

GCP 有三種 credential，各自用不同的身分發請求。

| Credential | 用誰的身分 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| OAuth 2.0 Client ID | 真人使用者 | 讓人登入你的 app，代他存取他的資料 |
| Service Account | 你的 app 自己 | 機器對機器，沒有使用者參與 |
| API Key | 誰的都不用，前端後端都一樣 | 呼叫 Maps 這類公開的 Google API |

選的時候依序問：

- 要一個真人按下「允許」→ **OAuth 2.0 Client ID**。
- 像 Maps 這種公開 API，不需要任何人的身分 → **API Key**，後端呼叫也一樣。
- 你的 app 用自己的身分去做事 → **Service Account**。

## OAuth 2.0 Client ID：代表使用者發請求

我是在做 Google 登入的時候碰到它的。那是 One Tap 的彈出視窗，Medium 也有，正式名稱叫 Google Identity Services。它要我填一個 OAuth 2.0 Client ID，我就搞糊塗了，因為我已經透過 Firebase Auth 在做 Google 登入，這兩個是不同的系統嗎？

其實不是。兩邊底下都是 OAuth 2.0 Client ID，差別只在串接方式，而且都要使用者自己走完登入流程。兩個還可以接在一起用：讓 One Tap 拿到 credential，再交給 Firebase Auth 管理。

```js
// 使用者主動登入
google.accounts.id.initialize({
  client_id: "YOUR-WEB-CLIENT-ID.apps.googleusercontent.com",
  callback: (response) => {
    // response.credential 是使用者的 ID token（一個 JWT），直接交給 Firebase
    firebase.auth().signInWithCredential(
      firebase.auth.GoogleAuthProvider.credential(response.credential)
    )
  },
})
```

**OAuth 的每個請求都代表一個使用者。** 使用者登入時，如果 app 申請了 offline access，後端會拿到一個 refresh token。之後使用者不在線上，後端也能用它換新的 access token。所以只要有人同意過一次，定時跑的後端其實可以一直用 OAuth 讀他的 calendar。

只是 server 的權限從此綁在這個人身上。[Google 的 OAuth 文件](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration)列了 refresh token 會失效的情況，例如使用者撤銷授權、token 六個月沒用過。app 的 consent screen 還在 Testing 狀態的話，refresh token 七天就過期。碰到任何一種，server 就讀不到 calendar，得再請那個人登入一次。

建立的路徑：GCP Console → APIs & Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID → 選 application type → 設定 authorized redirect URIs。

## Service Account：一個虛擬員工

機器對機器、中間沒有人的工作，就用這種 credential。Service Account（SA）像一個虛擬員工，有自己的身分（一個 email 地址），再替它設定權限。

我要讓後端用自己的身分讀*某一份特定*的 calendar，不借用任何使用者的授權，所以用 Service Account。

最後成功的流程：

1. 在 GCP 啟用 Calendar API。
2. 建一個 Service Account，也就是之後要拿來呼叫這個 API 的身分。
3. **把這個 SA 的 email 加進那份 calendar 的共用名單。**
4. 下載 SA 的 JSON key，把裡面的值放進環境變數，建立 auth client。

第一次我漏了第 3 步，其他設定看起來都對，API 卻一直失敗。我用這個 SA 實測過兩種情況。第一種，calendar 存在，只是沒有共用給 SA；第二種，calendar 根本不存在。API 兩種都回 `404 Not Found`，回應內容一模一樣。這跟 [Google 的 Calendar API 文件](https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/errors)寫的一致。所以如果 API 回了 404，先去看共用名單裡有沒有這個 SA。

SA 在 GCP 裡的權限再大，也讀不到沒共用給它的 calendar。就算在 GCP IAM（Identity and Access Management）給 SA 整個 project 的 Owner，結果也一樣。Calendar 是 Google Workspace 的 API（Gmail、Calendar、Drive 這一系列），讀取權限只看 calendar 自己的共用設定，GCP IAM 的角色涵蓋不到它。公司如果用 Workspace，還有另一個辦法：由 Workspace 的 super admin 開 domain-wide delegation，讓 SA 以組織裡的使用者身分存取資料。這個設定在 Workspace 的 Admin console，同樣不在 GCP IAM。

```js
function getGoogleAuth() {
  // 這三個值都來自下載的 SA JSON
  const clientEmail = process.env.GOOGLE_CLIENT_EMAIL
  const privateKey = process.env.GOOGLE_PRIVATE_KEY?.replace(/\\n/g, '\n') // 小心換行
  const projectId = process.env.GOOGLE_PROJECT_ID

  return new google.auth.GoogleAuth({
    credentials: { client_email: clientEmail, private_key: privateKey, project_id: projectId },
    scopes: ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar'],
  })
}

export function getCalendar() {
  return google.calendar({ version: 'v3', auth: getGoogleAuth() })
}
```

## API Key：公開服務的通行證

最後一種最單純。API Key 用在不碰任何人私人資料的公開 Google 服務，例如 Maps。

```js
// 沒帶 key：HTTP 200，但 body 寫 "status": "REQUEST_DENIED"
fetch(`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei`)

// 帶 key：拿得到結果，每月先扣免費額度
fetch(`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei&key=${API_KEY}`)
```

這把 key 跟身分沒什麼關係，它是拿來防濫用的：rate limit、追蹤用量、計費、限制哪些網站或 app 能用。AWS API Gateway 的 API key 也是同一個用途，讓服務方計算用量跟費用。

## 合起來看

一般的全端流程三種都會用到：

1. 前端用 **OAuth 2.0** 讓使用者登入。
2. 前端把使用者的 token 傳給後端驗證身分。
3. 後端用 **Service Account** 呼叫 Google 的服務。
4. 要用 Maps 這種公開服務，再加一把 **API Key**。

要選哪一種，照這個順序問：

```js
if (aRealUserMustConsent) return 'OAuth 2.0 Client ID'
if (noIdentityNeededLikeMaps) return 'API Key' // 就算是後端在呼叫也一樣
return 'Service Account' // 用你的 app 自己的身分
```

2. 在這台機器上跑過 `gcloud auth application-default login` 留下的檔案，裡面是登入那個人自己的 credential，不是 SA。
3. 程式執行環境上掛的 SA。GCP 的機器內建一個 metadata server，程式可以向它要這個 SA 的短期 token。

16:T39f8,:T52f6,<p>The "Sign in with Google" button on so many sites is OAuth 2.0. Later I needed a server to read a Google Calendar on a schedule, with no user signed in while it runs. Every OAuth request acts for a user who clicked "allow", so to use OAuth the server has to get one person to authorize it once and then keep borrowing that person's identity. That works, until the person revokes access or the token stops working, and then the server can't read the calendar. When the calendar doesn't belong to any user, the app's own identity fits better: a Service Account.</p>
<p>GCP has three credentials, and each one makes requests under a different identity.</p>

























<table><thead><tr><th>Credential</th><th>Whose identity</th><th>What it's for</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>OAuth 2.0 Client ID</td><td>a real user's</td><td>let people sign into your app, act on their data</td></tr><tr><td>Service Account</td><td>your app's own</td><td>machine to machine, no user involved</td></tr><tr><td>API Key</td><td>nobody's, from browser or backend</td><td>call a public Google API like Maps</td></tr></tbody></table>
<p>To choose, ask in this order:</p>
<ul>
<li>A real person has to click "allow" → <strong>OAuth 2.0 Client ID</strong>.</li>
<li>A public API like Maps that needs nobody's identity → <strong>API Key</strong>, even from your backend.</li>
<li>Your app acts as itself → <strong>Service Account</strong>.</li>
</ul>
<h2>OAuth 2.0 Client ID: requests made for a user</h2>
<p>I hit this building a Google sign-in (the One Tap popup, the kind Medium uses, officially Google Identity Services). It wanted an OAuth 2.0 Client ID. That confused me, because I was already doing Google login through Firebase Auth. Were they different systems?</p>
<p>They aren't. Both are OAuth 2.0 Client IDs underneath. They differ only in plumbing, and both need the user to walk through the sign-in flow. You can even chain them: let One Tap collect the credential, then hand it to Firebase Auth to manage:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// the user actively logs in</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">google.accounts.id.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">initialize</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  client_id: </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">"YOUR-WEB-CLIENT-ID.apps.googleusercontent.com"</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">,</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">  callback</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">: (</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#FFAB70;--shiki-light:#E36209">response</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">) </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">=></span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">    // response.credential is the user's ID token (a JWT), hand it straight to Firebase</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    firebase.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">auth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">().</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">signInWithCredential</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">      firebase.auth.GoogleAuthProvider.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">credential</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(response.credential)</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">    )</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  },</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">})</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p><strong>Every OAuth request acts for one user.</strong> If the app asks for offline access at sign-in, the backend gets a refresh token. After that, the backend can trade it for new access tokens while the user is offline. So once someone has consented, a scheduled backend can keep reading their calendar through OAuth.</p>
<p>The catch is that the server's access now depends on that one person. <a href="https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2#expiration">Google's OAuth documentation</a> lists the cases where a refresh token stops working, such as the user revoking access or the token going unused for six months. If the app's consent screen is still in Testing status, the refresh token expires in seven days. When any of these happens, the server can't read the calendar until that person signs in again.</p>
<p>To create one: GCP Console → APIs &#x26; Services → Credentials → Create Credentials → OAuth 2.0 Client ID → pick the application type → set the authorized redirect URIs.</p>
<h2>Service Account: a virtual employee</h2>
<p>This is the credential for machine to machine work, no human in the loop. A Service Account (SA) is a virtual employee: it has an identity (an email address), and you grant it permissions.</p>
<p>I wanted my backend to read one <em>specific</em> calendar under its own identity, without borrowing any user's authorization, so I used a Service Account.</p>
<p>The flow that finally worked:</p>
<ol>
<li>Enable the Calendar API in GCP.</li>
<li>Create a Service Account, the identity that will call that API.</li>
<li><strong>Add the SA's email to that calendar's share list.</strong></li>
<li>Download the SA's JSON key, pull the values into env vars, build the auth client.</li>
</ol>
<p>I skipped step 3 the first time. Everything else looked correct, and the API kept failing. I tested this with the same SA: a calendar that exists but isn't shared with it, and a calendar that doesn't exist at all, both return <code>404 Not Found</code> with identical bodies, as <a href="https://developers.google.com/workspace/calendar/api/guides/errors">Google's Calendar API docs</a> describe. So if the API returns 404, check the share list first.</p>
<p>No amount of GCP permission lets the SA read a calendar that isn't shared with it. Even if you give the SA Owner on the whole project in GCP IAM (Identity and Access Management), the result is the same. Calendar is a Google Workspace API (the Gmail, Calendar and Drive family): read access depends only on the calendar's own sharing settings, and GCP IAM roles don't cover it. If your company uses Workspace, there is one other route: a Workspace super admin turns on domain-wide delegation, which lets the SA act as users in the organization. That setting lives in the Workspace Admin console, also outside GCP IAM.</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">function</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1"> getGoogleAuth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">() {</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">  // these three come out of the downloaded SA JSON</span></span>

<h2>API Key: a permission slip for public stuff</h2>
<p>The last one is the simplest. An API Key is for public Google services that don't touch anyone's private data, like Maps.</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// no key: HTTP 200, but the body says "status": "REQUEST_DENIED"</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei`</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">)</span></span>
<span data-line=""> </span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// with key: results come back, billed against your monthly free usage first</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">fetch</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">(</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">`https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/geocode/json?address=Taipei&#x26;key=${</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5">API_KEY</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">}`</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">)</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>The key isn't really about identity. It's about abuse: rate limits, usage tracking, billing, restricting which sites or apps may use it. An API key on AWS API Gateway serves the same purpose: it lets the provider count how much you use and bill for it.</p>
<h2>Putting it together</h2>
<p>A typical full stack flow uses all three:</p>
<ol>
<li>Frontend logs the user in with <strong>OAuth 2.0</strong>.</li>
<li>Frontend passes the user's token to the backend to verify identity.</li>
<li>Backend uses a <strong>Service Account</strong> to talk to Google services.</li>
<li>Need a public service like Maps? Add an <strong>API Key</strong>.</li>
</ol>
<p>The decision, checked in this order:</p>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">if</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> (aRealUserMustConsent) </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">return</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> 'OAuth 2.0 Client ID'</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">if</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> (noIdentityNeededLikeMaps) </span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">return</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> 'API Key'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D"> // even when your backend calls it</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">return</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62"> 'Service Account'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D"> // your app acting as itself</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<h2>Do you have to download an SA key?</h2>
<p>Step 4 of the flow above downloads the SA's JSON key. By default that key never expires, and if it leaks, it works until someone revokes it.</p>
<p><strong>Deployed on GCP (Cloud Run, GCE, GKE):</strong> construct the client without passing a credential, and Google's SDK uses ADC (Application Default Credentials) to look in three places, in order, taking the first one it finds:</p>
<ol>
<li>The JSON file pointed to by the <code>GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS</code> env var.</li>
<li>The file left behind by running <code>gcloud auth application-default login</code> on this machine. It holds the credential of the person who signed in, not an SA.</li>
<li>The SA attached to where the code runs. GCP machines have a built-in metadata server, and the code can ask it for short-lived tokens for that SA.</li>
</ol>
<figure data-rehype-pretty-code-figure=""><pre tabindex="0" data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light"><code data-language="js" data-theme="github-dark github-light" style="display: grid;"><span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#6A737D;--shiki-light:#6A737D">// no credentials passed: ADC searches the three places above</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49">const</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#79B8FF;--shiki-light:#005CC5"> auth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> =</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#F97583;--shiki-light:#D73A49"> new</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E"> google.auth.</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#B392F0;--shiki-light:#6F42C1">GoogleAuth</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">({</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">  scopes: [</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#9ECBFF;--shiki-light:#032F62">'https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar'</span><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">],</span></span>
<span data-line=""><span style="--shiki-dark:#E1E4E8;--shiki-light:#24292E">})</span></span></code></pre></figure>
<p>On Cloud Run the first two usually don't exist, so ADC uses the third, and no key file is needed. If you don't name an SA when you deploy, Cloud Run attaches the Compute Engine default SA. For organizations created before 2024-05-03, or projects outside any organization, GCP may have automatically given that default SA the Editor role on the whole project. Anyone who breaks into the service can then use its identity to change most resources in the project. So create your own SA, give it only what it needs, and attach that one.</p>
<p>On your own machine, ADC usually stops at place 2 and uses the developer's own identity. If the developer owns the calendar, local reads always succeed, so a share list missing the SA causes no local error. You only find out after deploying, when the code runs as the SA and the API returns 404. To test locally as the SA, sign in with <code>gcloud auth application-default login --impersonate-service-account SA_EMAIL</code>. <a href="https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/authentication/use-service-account-impersonation">Google's impersonation docs</a> state that the developer's account needs <code>roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator</code> on that SA to do this.</p>
<p><strong>Deployed on a platform like Vercel:</strong> the machine isn't on GCP, there's no metadata server, and all three ADC places are empty. You have two options: put the key in env vars like the code above, or use <a href="https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/gcp">Vercel's OIDC (OpenID Connect) federation</a>. With OIDC, the code on Vercel gets a token signed by Vercel and exchanges it with GCP for a short-lived SA token, with no key anywhere.</p>
<p>Before GCP issues that token it checks two things, so set both up first:</p>
<ol>
<li>Was the token signed by a source GCP trusts? Create a Workload Identity Federation in GCP that trusts Vercel.</li>
<li>May this Vercel project use this SA? The federation turns the team, project and environment written in the token into an identity GCP recognizes (a principal), for example <code>principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/123456/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/vercel/subject/owner:my-team:project:my-app:environment:production</code>. Grant <code>roles/iam.serviceAccountUser</code> on the SA to that principal.</li>
</ol>
<p>The full setup steps are in <a href="https://vercel.com/docs/oidc/gcp">Vercel's docs</a>.</p>
<h2>Compared with AWS</h2>
<p>AWS and GCP wire up service permissions from opposite ends.</p>
<p>On AWS, nothing has access until you grant it. Create a Lambda in the console and, by default, it gets its own new execution role with only the basic logging permissions, like <code>CreateLogStream</code> and <code>PutLogEvents</code>. A second Lambda gets its own separate role by default, even if the permissions are identical. You are always the one saying "this function may touch that service."</p>
<p>GCP hands out permission by default. Every Cloud Run service you deploy without naming a service account shares the same Compute Engine default SA, and that SA may hold Editor on the whole project. With Editor, the service can read and write most GCP resources in the project with no extra grant. But Editor is a GCP IAM role, so to read a calendar the SA still has to be added to that calendar's share list.</p>8:["$","div",null,{"id":"root","children":["$","div",null,{"id":"main","className":"reading","children":["$","$L13",null,{"htmlContent":"$14","rawContent":"$15","base64Content":"$16","title":"GCP 的三種 credential：這個請求用誰的身分？","createdAt":"2025-09-08T21:28:00.000Z","updatedAt":"$undefined","tags":["cloud","gcp","auth","oauth"],"altHtmlContent":"$17","altTitle":"The three GCP credentials: whose identity does the request use?","currentLang":"zh","altLang":"en","canonicalPath":"/v2/three-gcp-credentials"}]}]}]
